title: 🔭 Mercury at Greatest Eastern Elongation — Evening Star
description: Mercury reaches its greatest angular separation from the Sun (18.1°), making this the best window to spot the innermost planet. Look for it low in the western sky shortly after sunset. Look west after sunset — Mercury sets or rises with the twilight and is only visible for a short window. It never strays far from the Sun in our sky.

title: 🔭 Venus at Greatest Eastern Elongation — Evening Star
description: Venus reaches its greatest angular separation from the Sun (45.9°) — the best viewing opportunity of this apparition. Find it low in the western sky shortly after sunset, shining brilliantly at magnitude −4 or brighter, far outshining every other star and planet. Look west after sunset and it will be unmistakable.
